entities.name: Amyntas IV of Macedon
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Amyntas IV of Macedon was a titular king of the Greek kingdom of Macedonia in 359 BC and member of the Argead dynasty.

He ascended to the throne at the age of 20 after the death of his father, Amyntas III, and immediately began consolidating power.

In 358 BC, Amyntas IV launched a successful campaign against the neighboring Thracian tribes, which led to the expansion of Macedonian territory and increased its economic influence in the region.

Amyntas IV's military successes were bolstered by his close relationship with Philip II, who would later become king and play a crucial role in uniting Macedonia under a single ruler.

The legacy of Amyntas IV can be seen in the continued growth and prosperity of Macedonia, which would eventually rise to become one of the dominant powers in ancient Greece.

As the sun set on his 50-year reign, Amyntas IV left behind a kingdom that was more powerful than ever before, with its economy thriving and its military strength unmatched.
